question.leadin: Ozan Kilinc ("KILL-inch") was jailed by a court in this country for publishing articles sympathetic to a banned party.
question.text: Name this country, where insulting the country or the government is illegal under Article 301.
question.clue: The Simav and Nilufer Rivers flow into its Sea of Marmara.

swap.leadin: The Golden Horn cuts into this city and was once spanned by a large chain to prevent enemy ships from getting in.
swap.text: Name this Turkish city that was previously named Byzantium and Constantinople.
swap.clue: Cannons designed by the Hungarian engineer Orban were used to breach this city's Theodosian Walls.

question.leadin: A huge amount of impressive building projects were designed by this ruler's architect, Sinan.
question.text: Name this son of Selim the Grim, who won the Battle of Mohacs [Moe-HOTCH] but was less successful in conquering Malta and also led an unsuccessful siege of Vienna.
question.answerHtml: Suleiman the Magnificent [or Suleiman the Lawgiver or Suleiman I; prompt on “Suleiman”]
question.clue: At the Battle of Mohacs, this ruler's forces killed Louis II, after which this ruler threw his support behind John Zapolya.

swap.text: In the 1910s and 20s, the Young Turks perpetrated a genocide on this ethnic group, in which the Ottoman Empire forced this group from their homeland. The modern Turkish government refuses to identify the event as a genocide.
swap.answerHtml: Armenians (accept Armenian genocide or Armenian Holocaust, but do not prompt on Holocaust)
swap.clue: Thanks to Gregory the Illuminator, these people had the world's first official Christian state starting in 301.

question.leadin: Many of those who orchestrated this event were assassinated during Operation Nemesis.
question.text: Identify this event in which over a million people of a certain Caucasian nationality were forcibly resettled and killed, perpetrated by the Ottoman Empire during World War I.
question.answerHtml: Armenian Genocide (accept equivalents like Armenian Massacre; prompt on “Great Crime” or “Medz Yeghern”)
question.clue: Henry Morgenthau, Sr. was unable to coax the United States into intervening in this event, which began on Red Sunday and was opposed in the city of Van.

swap.text: After the dissolution of the Black Army, this Ottoman sultan and husband of Hurrem Sultan, also known as Roxelana, conquered Hungary in the Battle of Mohacs.
swap.answerHtml: Suleiman I (accept Suleiman the Magnificent, accept Suleiman the Lawgiver; prompt on Suleiman)
swap.clue: This ruler expelled the Knights Hospitalers from Rhodes after conquering Belgrade, although the same group would defeat him at Malta later on.

question.text: Ottoman Sultan Murad IV bulldozed coffeehouses to prevent these people from conspiring against him. This military force recruited from the Devshirme("dave-SHEER-may") system was abolished under the Tanzimat reforms.
question.clue: In a coronation ceremony for a monarch sometimes called "The Sot" or "The Drunkard", this group refused to march to the Topkapi Palace until bribed, and they originally served as a bodyguard for Orkhan.

swap.text: The Janissaries were disbanded before this period of 19th-century reforms, which began with the Rescript of the Rose Chamber. Its modernizing provisions included ending a tax on non-Muslims and nationalizing the census.
swap.clue: The Rescript of the Rose Chamber promised the end of tax farming during this period, during which changes in the millet system attempted to curb nationalism among religious minorities.

question.leadin: Shortly after his greatest victory, this ruler executed his vizier Candarli Halil Pasha.
question.text: Name this Ottoman sultan whose second reign lasted from 1451 until 1481. His greatest military feat was aided by massive cannons designed by a Hungarian named Orban.
question.answerHtml: Mehmed II [or Mehmed the Conqueror or Mehmet II or Mehmet the Conqueror or Mahomet II or Mahomet the Conqueror]
question.clue: This ruler established a millet led by Gennadius II, who received authority over all Orthodox Christians in his empire.

swap.leadin: Name these things related to post-World War II economic booms.
swap.text: An alternative to the Marshall Plan that helped spark Europe's economic recovery was one named after a Secretary of the Treasury of this name, who advocated the deindustrialization of Germany. Another person with this name was the Ottoman Ambassador for the US during the Armenian Genocide and its most prominent opponent.
swap.clue: Another man with this surname called for a namesake plan urging that postwar Germany be ruthlessly partitioned into separate, agrarian states.

question.text: After the Turkish nationalists rallied to defeat the Greeks, Armenians, and French, this new treaty replaced, and returned all of the concessions of, Sevres.
question.clue: An earlier treaty signed at the same location was also called the Treaty of Ouchy, and ended the Italo-Turkish War in 1912.

swap.text: After the final dissolution of the Ottoman Empire, this man led the new nation of Turkey starting in 1922.
swap.answerHtml: Mustafa <u>Kemal</u> <u>Ataturk</u> [accept either underlined portion; or Mustafa Kemal <u>Pasha</u>]
swap.clue: This man's opposition to the Treaty of Sevres led to its replacement with the Treaty of Lausanne.

question.text: In 1845, a holder of this title wrote the treatise "Benefits to Children" describing vaccine efforts for a cowpox outbreak. Holders of this Ottoman title like Enver and Cemal ["jamal"] led a "Young Turk Triumvirate" shadow government until the empire's collapse post-WWI.
question.clue: The genocide was carried out by the Committee of Union and Progress under three de facto leaders with this title. Talaat and Ahmed Cemal ("keh-mal"), who both had this title, were assassinated for their role in the genocide during Operation Nemesis.

swap.leadin: A "protocol" named for this city called for Israel to invade Egypt, after which Britain and France would issue disingenuous statements that they had to seize the Suez Canal to maintain its neutrality.
swap.text: Name this French city. A treaty named for this city confirmed an armistice signed in Moudros Harbor and divided a country into Italian, French, British, and Greek zones of occupation.

question.text: Soon after the Auspicious Incident, the Ottoman army was modernized during this wider initiative. The introduction of paper money and post offices, as well as units called vilayets, were among the changes introduced during this initiative.
question.clue: The Young Turk Revolution established the Ottoman Empire's second constitutional era; the first constitution put an end to this period of moderate reform that lasted from the 1839 Edict of Gulhane (gool-HAH-neh) to 1876.

swap.text: After their defeat and the occupation of Istanbul, the Ottoman government was forced to sign this treaty in 1920. It partitioned the empire and proposed dividing much of the remaining Turkish territory into foreign spheres of influence.
swap.clue: This treaty formalized the territory divisions laid out four months prior at the San Remo Conference, as well the earlier end of hostilities in the Armistice of Mudros.

question.leadin: At the end of this novel, Gabriel Bagradian is killed while standing over his son's grave, but not before he manages to get his fellow townsmen on a ship.
question.text: Identify this novel set during the Armenian genocide, in which the Turks attempt to seize the title mountain.
question.answerHtml: The Forty Days of Musa Dagh [or Die vierzig Tage des Musa Dagh]
question.answer: The Forty Days of Musa Dagh

swap.leadin: Description acceptable. An elaborate Surname("soor-nah-MEH") that depicts parading glassworkers was created to celebrate the 1582 circumcision of a holder of this title.
swap.text: Give this title, whose holders were raised in seclusion as part of the kafes("kah-FESS") system. Roxelana engineered the 1553 execution of a holder of this title.
swap.answerHtml: şehzade (“shay-zah-DEH”) [or shâhzâde (“shah-zah-DEH”); accept Ottoman crown prince or heir-apparent to the Ottoman Empire; prompt on crown prince or heir-apparent by asking “in which Empire?”; prompt on children of the Ottoman Sultan or children of the Ottoman Emperor; reject “Ottoman Sultan,” “Ottoman Emperor,” or “Ottoman Caliph”]

question.text: This overall commander of Ottoman forces at Beersheba later received a surname drawn from the two 1921 battles where he forced invading Greeks to retreat. He was the successor of Ataturk as the second President of Turkey.
question.clue: The implementer of the Turkish surname law, Mustafa Kemal, took the surname Ataturk, while this "National Chief" who succeeded him took his surname from a town where he fought during the Greco-Turkish War.

swap.leadin: Identify the following related to the military career of Eugene of Savoy, FTPE.
swap.text: Prince Euguene's decisive victory over the Ottomans in this September 1697 battle was a major factor in forcing the Ottomans to accept the Peace of Karlowitz two years later.
swap.clue: At this 1697 battle, Eugene of Savoy led a surprise attack on an Ottoman force attempting to cross the Tisza river. The result was a rout in which the Austrians inflicted over 30,000 casualties on the Ottomans.
